This request is for authorization to apply for the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant through the
Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency (GEMA/HS). Awarded funds
are used to enhance the County’s cybersecurity monitoring and incident response and strengthen
the protection of County computer systems, network infrastructure, data, and critical operations.

Motion by _____________, second by _______________ and carried _______________ to

     approve


     disapprove


     table


     authorize

the MIS Department to apply for FY2025 State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program
funding through GEMA/HS in the amount of $112,533.62, with a required County match
of $75,022.41. The County’s match is already included in the MIS operating budget and
represents funds that are allocated to existing cybersecurity services

Houston County Board of Commissioners
                                     Management Information Systems
                                               Will Davis, Director
                                              200 Carl Vinson Parkway
                                              Warner Robins, GA 31093
                                               Phone: 478-542-2030

                                           MEMORANDUM

To: Houston County Board of Commissioners
From: Will Davis – Director of Management Information Systems
Date: 10/13/2026
Re: Request for Approval – GEMA/HS State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Application


The Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency (GEMA/HS) administer the State and
Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP), a federally funded program that helps state and local governments
strengthen their cybersecurity. The MIS Department is requesting approval to apply for FY2025 funding to
enhance the County’s cybersecurity monitoring and incident response capabilities.
The grant requires a 40 percent local cost share, and funded projects must align with the Georgia Cybersecurity
Plan. Grant funding would offset a portion of the cost of enhanced cybersecurity services, improving the
County’s ability to detect threats, respond to incidents, and reduce the potential financial and operational
impacts of a security incident.
Staff requests approval to apply for $112,533.62 in federal grant funding, with a required local match of
$75,022.41, for a total project cost of $187,556.03. The County’s matching funds are included in the MIS
operating budget; therefore, no additional appropriation is required during the initial grant period. Following the
grant period, continued funding for these services would be requested through an increase to the MIS operating
budget.




Respectfully,




Will Davis
Director, Management Information Systems

   Commissioner Byrd
The MIS Department has identified an email gateway security solution from Proofpoint, Inc. that
offers comparable protection at a lower cost than the County’s current annual agreement with
Barracuda Networks. These services protect County email accounts from phishing, spam, and
malware.

     table

the quotes from CDW-G, procured through State of Georgia Software Contract, totaling
$66,163.50 with implementation services provided at no additional cost, and authorize the
MIS Department to enter into an annual agreement with Proofpoint, Inc. for email security
services. This purchase is included in the existing operating budgets for software
subscriptions and results in an annual savings of $53,960.34.

Houston County Board of Commissioners
                                           Management Information Systems
                                                  Will Davis, Director
                                                 200 Carl Vinson Parkway
                                                 Warner Robins, GA 31093
                                                  Phone: 478-542-2030


                                               MEMORANDUM

To: Houston County Board of Commissioners
From: Will Davis – Director of Management Information Systems
Date: 10/09/2026
Re: Request for Approval – Email Security Quote


The MIS Department utilizes an email gateway security solution through an annual subscription with Barracuda
Networks to protect County email accounts from phishing attempts, spam, and malware. The renewal for the term
beginning October 18, 2026, was quoted at $120,123.84.
Prior to renewing the existing subscription, MIS staff evaluated the County’s current email security services to ensure
they continued to meet the County’s needs and provide the best value. Through this review, staff identified a solution
from Proofpoint, Inc., that offers comparable protection at a substantially lower annual cost. The proposed Proofpoint
subscription is quoted at $66,163.50, resulting in annual savings of $53,960.34.
Staff recommends approval of the quote from CDW-G in the amount of $66,163.50 and authorization to enter into an
annual agreement with Proofpoint, Inc., for email security services. The quote is provided through State of Georgia
Software Contract SPD0000060-0004. The agreement includes implementation services at no additional cost. This
purchase is included in existing operating budgets for software subscriptions.

Houston County Office of Coroner

James Robert “Jimbob” Williams, Coroner

200 Carl Vinson Parkway Warner Robins, Georgia 31088
Office- 478-542-2113 Cell- 478-955-2412

To: Houston County Board of Commissioners Office
From: Coroner James Williams

Date: October 7, 2026

Ref: Vehicle Purchase Request

1 respectfully request approval to have the purchasing department purchase a new vehicle to replace Unit 932, which as a
retired 2013 Ford F-150 from the Houston County Sheriff's Office that our office has been using for an extended amount of
time. That unit was dead lined earlier this year due to major repairs that were needed (estimated over $4,500.00). Based on the

number of repairs and vehicle having over 172,000 miles, the repairs were not completed.

I recommend purchasing a 2026 Chevrolet Silverado RST from Hamby Chevrolet in Perry, Georgia for the price of
$57,138.20. This vehicle will be used to respond to death scenes, transport needed crime scene processing equipment,
transport evidence to and from the medical examiner’s office in Atlanta, Pooler, and Macon and other coroner duties. This
vehicle is available for purchase now and would better suit our office for operational needs. This purchase will be funded by

2018 SPLOST.

I have included the quote from Hamby Chevrolet to the purchasing department along with other dealer quote comparisons.

Thank you for your consideration, respectfully,

A

James R. Williams

Houston County Coroner

    October 9, 2026

    TO: Chairman Dan Perdue, Houston County Board of Commissioners
    TO: Ken Carter, Director of Personnel
    FROM: Sheriff Matt Moulton
    RE: Request for Authorization to Hire – 911 Systems Manager

    Chairman Perdue and Mr. Carter,

    I am writing to respectfully request authorization to hire Mr. Josiah Miller as the Systems
    Manager for the Houston County 911 Center.

    Our current Systems Manager, Mr. Tim Ealer, has announced his decision to retire effective
    November 30, 2026. This position is critical to the daily operations of the Houston County 911
    Center, as well as the numerous public safety agencies that depend on the systems and services
    supported by the 911 Center. Maintaining the reliability and functionality of these systems is
    essential to ensuring that our first responders have the resources necessary to serve and protect
    the citizens of Houston County.

    I believe Mr. Miller possesses the experience, qualifications, and technical knowledge
    necessary to successfully fulfill the responsibilities of this position. I respectfully request
    authorization to hire Mr. Miller as soon as possible to allow him the opportunity to work
    alongside Mr. Ealer prior to his retirement. This transition period will provide Mr. Miller with
    valuable firsthand experience regarding Mr. Ealer's daily responsibilities, as well as the
    opportunity to become familiar with the specialized systems and operations of our 911 Center.

    I cannot overstate the importance of ensuring a smooth transition in this position. Allowing Mr.
    Miller to work directly with Mr. Ealer for the next several weeks will help preserve institutional
    knowledge, minimize potential disruptions, and ensure continuity of operations for the 911
    Center and the public safety agencies we support.

    Based on Mr. Miller's experience and qualifications, I respectfully request authorization to hire
    him at Pay Grade 25, Step E, with an hourly rate of $36.75.

    I appreciate your consideration of this request and your continued support of the Houston
    County Sheriff's Office and our 911 Center. I believe this is a necessary and proactive step to
    ensure that we maintain the high level of service our citizens and public safety partners expect
    and deserve.

Respectfully,

Matt Moulton
Matt Moulton
Sheriff, Houston County, Georgia
